slides.headline: October 15, 1931: a fisherman's son was born in Rameswaram. He would go on to run India's missile program and its presidency.
Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam was born in Rameswaram, Tamil Nadu
slides.body: He joined DRDO in 1958 and moved to ISRO in 1969, where he served as Project Director for India's first satellite launch vehicle, SLV-III - before returning to DRDO to lead the development of missiles like Agni and Prithvi.

slides.headline: He played a central role in India's 1998 Pokhran-II nuclear tests, then became the country's 11th President.
slides.body: He served as President from 2002 to 2007, elected with backing from both the ruling and opposition parties. He received the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian honour, in 1997.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat needs scientists who can also lead institutions.
slides.body: Kalam's path - from a fisherman's son to missile scientist to President - showed that India's highest offices could be reached through technical achievement, not just political careers.
